title: Nneka Ogwumike Announces WNBA Retirement and Leaves Her Mark on the League
seoTitle: Nneka Ogwumike Announces WNBA Retirement After 15 Seasons
subtitle: The veteran player wraps up her fifteen-season career after making basketball history.
excerpt: Discover the details about player Nneka Ogwumike's retirement, her successful career trajectory, and her impact on the sport.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Player Nneka Ogwumike has announced that she is retiring from the league after the season. The announcement caught fans and peers by surprise, marking the end of a fifteen-season run on the court.

Career and records on the court

The athlete was the first overall draft pick and accumulated awards over the years, including the regular-season Most Valuable Player title and a championship won with the Los Angeles Sparks. She also set the franchise's all-time scoring record and participated in multiple All-Star games, maintaining a high level of play without a drop in performance.

The decision to return to Los Angeles

In April, the athlete had announced her intention to re-sign with the Los Angeles team for the season, the squad where she spent the first twelve seasons of her career. Teammates pointed out that she was still playing at a high level and posting MVP-caliber numbers, which sparked surprise at her decision to stop playing now.

Off-court leadership and the collective bargaining agreement

In addition to her athletic success, her tenure as president of the players association was marked by important negotiations to improve contracts and benefits for the category. Peers highlighted her dedication and preparedness in negotiation topics, securing better conditions and compensation for the league's athletes.

Recognition from professional peers

Several athletes and coaches paid tribute in recent weeks, highlighting the constant support she offered to younger players. The mentorship relationship and the psychological and technical support given to rising names were fondly remembered by colleagues from various teams.

With information from USA Today.
